policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment / Shared Housing Establishment (all staff, contractors, volunteers and students)
policies.purpose: To protect the privacy and confidentiality of resident information, to state when HIPAA applies to [AGENCY NAME], and to ensure residents and their representatives can obtain copies of their assessments and service plan.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps each resident's personal, health, financial and service information confidential. It releases that information only as this policy allows. This applies whether or not HIPAA covers the establishment. HIPAA applies only to the extent [AGENCY NAME] or its providers are covered entities. Counsel makes that determination in writing, and the Administrator keeps it on file. If [AGENCY NAME] is a covered entity, it also follows the federal privacy standards listed above, including the minimum-necessary rule, the uses and disclosures rules and the administrative requirements. On request, the resident or the resident's representative receives a copy of the latest comprehensive assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the current service plan.

definitions.definition: A health plan, health care clearinghouse, or health care provider that transmits health information electronically in connection with standard transactions covered by HIPAA. Counsel decides whether [AGENCY NAME] or any provider it uses falls in this group.
Any information that identifies a resident and relates to the resident's health, care, services, finances, or residency, in any form (paper, electronic or oral).
Using or sharing only the amount of information needed for a task, where that standard applies.
The person the resident has designated, or who is legally authorized, to act for the resident (see RR-09).

procedures: Before opening, the Administrator asks counsel to determine whether [AGENCY NAME], or any provider it employs or contracts with, is a HIPAA covered entity. The Administrator files the written determination in the compliance file and repeats the review annually and whenever billing or service arrangements change (for example, when the establishment begins billing electronically).
The Administrator designates a Privacy Contact in writing ([PRIVACY CONTACT NAME], [PHONE]) to answer questions, receive complaints about privacy and oversee this policy.

If counsel finds [AGENCY NAME] is a covered entity, the Privacy Contact adopts and posts the required Notice of Privacy Practices. The Privacy Contact also gives the notice to each resident or representative at admission and obtains a signed acknowledgment, and maintains the authorization, accounting and complaint procedures required by the federal rules.
Each employee, volunteer and contractor signs a confidentiality agreement at hire. The Administrator keeps it in the personnel file (STF-05).

Staff access resident information only as needed for their job. Charts are kept in a locked cabinet or room or in a password-protected electronic system. Staff do not leave records open or unattended on counters, in hallways or on screens.

Staff do not discuss residents' health, behavior or finances in common areas, dining rooms or with visitors, other residents or anyone off site. Staff do not post resident health information where visitors can see it.

Staff release resident information outside the establishment only (a) with the written authorization of the resident or representative, or (b) as required or permitted by law, such as abuse reporting (SAF-01), reports to IDPH (REC-02), access by the Long-Term Care Ombudsman (RR-03), public health reporting (SAF-09), or sharing with treating providers and emergency responders for the resident's care. Staff consult the Administrator when unsure.
Staff verify the identity and authority of any caller or visitor requesting information. They do not give information by phone to unverified persons.
Staff do not photograph or record residents without written consent from the resident or representative. Staff may not post resident images or information on social media.

A resident or representative may request a copy of the latest comprehensive assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the service plan, orally or in writing. The staff member receiving the request notifies the Administrator the same day. As an agency standard, the Administrator provides the copies within 5 business days, free of charge, and records the date of the request and the date provided.
Where a request comes from a representative, staff first verify the representative's authority using the documentation on file (RR-09).

Staff report any suspected improper use or disclosure of resident information (misdirected fax or email, lost record, unauthorized access) to the Privacy Contact the same day. The Privacy Contact investigates, documents the facts and corrective action, notifies the affected resident or representative, and makes any notifications required by law or by counsel.
Electronic records require unique user IDs and passwords. Staff do not share passwords. The Administrator removes system access on the day a staff member leaves.
Records are retained, stored and destroyed in accordance with REC-01. Destroyed paper records are shredded.
The Administrator provides privacy training at orientation and annually thereafter (STF-03) and documents attendance.

[AGENCY NAME] does not retaliate against any resident or staff member who raises a privacy concern or files a complaint. Staff who violate this policy are subject to discipline up to and including termination (STF-06).

responsibilities.duty: Obtains the covered-entity determination from counsel, designates the Privacy Contact, enforces this policy, and fulfills copy requests.
Handles questions and complaints, investigates suspected improper disclosures, and maintains privacy notices and authorizations if HIPAA applies.
Protect resident information, sign the confidentiality agreement, complete privacy training and report suspected breaches immediately.
Determines HIPAA covered-entity status and advises on disclosure questions.

documentation: Written covered-entity determination and annual review
Privacy Contact designation
Signed staff confidentiality agreements
Notice of Privacy Practices acknowledgments (if applicable)
Resident authorizations for release of information
Log of requests for copies of assessments and service plans, with dates requested and provided
Privacy incident reports and corrective action records
Privacy training attendance records

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment / Shared Housing Establishment (admissions, marketing, resident care and all staff)
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d)
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] treats applicants and residents fairly, applies the Act's age definition consistently, makes reasonable accommodations for disability, and provides interpretation and translation for residents with limited English proficiency.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate against any applicant or resident on the basis of race, color, national origin, language, religion, sex, disability or any other basis prohibited by law. Admission and retention decisions are based on the resident's care needs, the establishment's ability to meet them, and the criteria in ADM-01 and ADM-04. The Act and Part 295 require that at least 80% of residents be age 55 or older. [AGENCY NAME] applies this definitional rule the same way in marketing and in admission decisions. It does not use it to treat applicants differently on any other basis. [AGENCY NAME] provides reasonable accommodations for residents with disabilities, as the ADA requires. To the extent [AGENCY NAME] receives federal financial assistance, it follows Title VI. It gives residents with limited English proficiency free interpretation and translated copies of key documents.

definitions.definition: A limited ability to read, speak, write or understand English well enough to take part in care and decisions without language help.

A change in rules, policies, practices or services that gives a person with a disability an equal opportunity to use and enjoy the establishment, when the change does not impose an undue burden or fundamentally alter the services.
The establishment contract, the resident rights list, the grievance process, the service plan, the discharge/transfer notice, and any consent or risk agreement.

procedures: The Administrator posts and distributes a nondiscrimination statement in the admissions packet and in the lobby, in the languages most commonly used by residents and applicants.
Marketing materials, tours and inquiry responses are given equally to all inquirers. Staff do not steer, discourage or screen out inquirers on prohibited bases.

Before each admission, the Administrator documents the age of the applicant and confirms that, with the applicant, at least 80% of residents will be age 55 or older. If an admission would drop the establishment below that level, the Administrator documents the finding and does not admit without first getting advice from counsel or IDPH.
Admission denials are based only on documented care needs or the criteria in ADM-01 and ADM-04. The reasons are given to the applicant in writing and filed.
At the first contact, staff ask each applicant and resident for the language in which they prefer to receive health and service information. They record the answer in the record.

When a resident or representative has LEP, the Administrator arranges a qualified interpreter (in person, by phone, or by video) at no cost. [AGENCY NAME] uses a family member or another resident to interpret only if the resident asks, and the request is documented. Staff do not use minors as interpreters except in an emergency.

The Administrator provides translated copies of key documents or has a qualified interpreter read them aloud and records that this was done. This includes the contract, rights list, grievance process and service plan.
The Administrator maintains a list of interpreter and translation resources, including phone or video services, and posts it at the nurses' station or staff office.
For residents with sensory or communication disabilities, staff provide appropriate aids, such as large print, written notes, amplification or sign language interpretation.

A resident or applicant with a disability may request an accommodation orally or in writing. The Administrator responds within 5 business days (agency standard), documents the request and the decision, and gives the reasons for any denial and any alternative offered.
Staff do not retaliate against anyone who requests an accommodation, uses an interpreter, or files a discrimination complaint. Complaints are handled under RR-02.

The Administrator confirms the state-level nondiscrimination language in Part 295 and the Act's resident rights list. The Administrator then updates this policy and the admissions packet if they contain requirements not reflected here and records the date of that review in the compliance file.
The Administrator trains all staff on this policy at hire and annually (STF-03), including how to obtain an interpreter.
The Administrator reviews admission and denial decisions and language-access requests at least annually as part of the quality improvement program (GOV-04) and documents any corrective action.

responsibilities.duty: Applies admission criteria consistently, tracks the 55+ composition, approves accommodations, arranges interpreters and translation, and reviews this policy.
Treat all inquirers equally, record language preference and age, and document reasons for any denial.
Use interpreters, honor accommodations, and report discrimination concerns to the Administrator.

documentation: Nondiscrimination statement
Age and 55+ composition record at each admission
Written admission denial notices with reasons
Language preference recorded in each resident record
Interpreter use log and translated document records
Accommodation request and decision forms
Annual review of admissions decisions and language access in QI minutes
Training attendance records

policies.title: Resident's Representative
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment / Shared Housing Establishment (admissions, nursing, service planning, dementia program and all staff)
policies.purpose: To ensure each resident can designate a representative, that the designation is recorded, and that the representative takes part in the contract, service plan and decisions to the extent the resident wishes or the law provides.
policies.policy: Each resident may designate a representative. The establishment contract lists the resident's designated representative, and the representative takes part in agreeing to the service plan. A resident in a dementia program must have a designated representative. [AGENCY NAME] verifies the representative's authority, records it, and deals with the representative within that authority. A resident who has capacity keeps the right to make personal decisions and to take part in decisions affecting his or her care. [AGENCY NAME] follows the Department's rule on the resident's representative. The Administrator confirms that this policy matches the current text of that rule.

definitions.definition: A person designated by the resident, or authorized by law or court order (for example, an agent under a power of attorney or a guardian), to act on the resident's behalf to the extent of that authority.
A special program or unit the establishment offers for residents with Alzheimer's disease or a related dementia and that it has disclosed to IDPH and to residents.
The designation form, power of attorney, guardianship order or other legal paper that shows the representative's authority.

procedures: During pre-admission screening (ADM-01), the Admissions staff ask each applicant whether he or she wishes to name a representative, and who it should be. This is recorded in the admission file.

The applicant or resident completes the Resident Representative Designation Form ([FORM NUMBER]) with the representative's name, relationship, address, phone and email, and the scope of authority. If the resident cannot complete it because of cognitive impairment, staff ask for the legal authority document, such as a power of attorney or guardianship order, and file a copy.

The Administrator reviews the authority documents. If the documents do not clearly establish authority, the Administrator asks for clarification from the resident or counsel before relying on the representative for any decision.

The representative is entered in the establishment contract (RR-04) as the resident's designated representative, with a phone number for emergencies and notifications. The representative signs the contract with the resident when authorized or required.

For a resident admitted to the dementia program, the Administrator does not complete admission until a representative has been designated and recorded (HCS-05). If no representative exists, the Administrator works with the resident, family and, if needed, counsel or the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, and documents the efforts.

The Nurse or Administrator invites the resident and the representative to take part in the assessment review and in agreeing to the service plan (ADM-02, ADM-03). The representative's participation, or the invitation declined, is noted in the service plan record.

Staff give the representative notice of changes of condition, incidents, fee changes, discharge or transfer notices, and other matters the resident has authorized or the law requires (HCS-04, SAF-02, RR-04, ADM-05).
The representative receives copies of the latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment and service plan on request (RR-07).

Staff communicate directly with the resident and honor the resident's wishes whenever the resident can express them, even if a representative is on file. Staff do not treat the existence of a representative as removing the resident's rights (RR-01).

No employee or owner of [AGENCY NAME] may serve as a resident's representative unless the Administrator documents the reason and has confirmed with counsel that it is permitted and conflicts are addressed. Staff may not accept gifts, loans or financial benefits from a representative or resident (STF-06).

If staff believe a representative is not acting in the resident's best interest, staff report to the Administrator the same day. The Administrator follows SAF-01 where abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected, and may contact the Long-Term Care Ombudsman (RR-03) or Adult Protective Services as appropriate.

The resident may change or revoke the designation at any time while able to do so. The Administrator updates the contract by a written change signed by both parties (RR-04), updates the record and notifies staff.
The Administrator reviews each resident's representative information at the annual reassessment and updates contact details. The Administrator documents that the review occurred.
The Administrator checks the current text of the Department's rule on the resident's representative at least annually, and updates this policy and the forms if the rule has changed.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies authority documents, ensures a representative is designated for every dementia program resident, and updates this policy to match the rule.
Offer the designation at pre-admission, collect the form and documents, and enter the representative in the contract.
Involve the representative in service plan agreement and notify the representative of changes.
Know who each resident's representative is, honor the resident's own wishes, and report concerns about a representative.

documentation: Resident Representative Designation Form
Copies of power of attorney, guardianship or other authority documents
Representative listed in the signed establishment contract
Service plan signature or participation record
Notification records to the representative
Written revocation or change of designation
Annual review record

policies.title: Essential Support Persons
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment / Shared Housing Establishment (all residents, visitors and staff)
policies.purpose: To allow each resident to designate an essential support person and to keep that person's access in place, including during outbreaks or other restrictions, consistent with the Department's rule on essential support persons.
policies.policy: A resident, or the resident's representative, may designate one or more essential support persons. [AGENCY NAME] follows the Department's rule on essential support persons for the designation process, access conditions and documentation. This policy is to be conformed to the text of that rule before adoption. The Administrator performs this check and records the date. [AGENCY NAME] will not impose limits on an essential support person's access that are stricter than that rule permits. It will not limit access as a way to avoid providing care or services. Under the ADA, [AGENCY NAME] makes reasonable modifications when a resident with a disability needs a support person in order to take part in care or services.

definitions.definition: A person the resident (or the resident's representative) designates, such as a family member, friend or other person, who provides emotional, social or care support that is important to the resident's well-being, as the Department's rule defines and allows.
The Essential Support Person Designation Form (Attachment RR-10-A) that records the resident's choice.
A time when the establishment limits visitor access for health, safety or emergency reasons, such as a communicable disease outbreak or a declared emergency.

procedures: Before adoption of this manual, the Administrator obtains the current text of the Department's rule on essential support persons. The Administrator verifies the designation process, access conditions (including during outbreaks or restrictions), and documentation requirements, and updates this policy and Attachment RR-10-A to match. The Administrator records the review date in the compliance file.

At admission and in the resident rights review (RR-01), staff tell each resident and representative that the resident may designate essential support persons. This information is also included in the admissions packet.

A resident or representative may designate an essential support person at admission or at any later time by completing Attachment RR-10-A. The form records the resident's name, the person's name, relationship, phone, the type of support provided, and the resident's or representative's signature and date.

If the resident cannot sign, the representative signs (RR-09). If the resident has no representative and cannot express a choice, staff document the resident's known wishes from family and the care team, and the Administrator decides with guidance from the Long-Term Care Ombudsman or counsel when needed.

The Administrator reviews the completed form within 2 business days (agency standard), enters the person on the resident's visitor and support list, and informs shift staff who work with the resident.

The Administrator provides the essential support person with a copy of the visitor guidelines. These include sign-in procedures, health screening, infection prevention steps, and safety rules. They are applied to the essential support person only as the rule allows.

Staff allow the essential support person access to the resident as the Department's rule provides, including during any restriction period. Staff do not deny entry unless the Administrator has documented a safety reason allowed by the rule.

During an outbreak or other restriction (SAF-07, SAF-09, SAF-05), the Administrator tells essential support persons how to enter safely. This includes screening, hand hygiene, personal protective equipment, and the areas they may visit. The Administrator documents the restriction, the decision and the date.

If an essential support person breaks safety rules, the Administrator talks with the person and, where needed, sets written conditions that the Department's rule allows. The Administrator documents each step and informs the resident and representative.
A resident or representative may remove or change an essential support person at any time. The Administrator updates the form and the support list on the same day.
Staff report to the Administrator any concern about an essential support person's conduct. If abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected, staff follow SAF-01 immediately.

A resident or essential support person who disagrees with an access decision may file a grievance (RR-02) or contact the Long-Term Care Ombudsman (RR-03). The Administrator reviews every such complaint.
The Administrator reviews denials or limits on essential support persons' access at least quarterly through the quality improvement program (GOV-04) and documents any corrective action.

responsibilities.duty: Conforms this policy and form to the Department's rule, approves designations, manages access during restrictions and reviews denials.
Tell residents about the right to designate an essential support person and help complete the form.
Know each resident's essential support persons, allow access as permitted and report concerns.

documentation: Essential Support Person Designation Form (Attachment RR-10-A)
Resident visitor and support list
Record of the Administrator's review of the Department's rule text
Restriction period decisions and notices to essential support persons
Records of any access conditions or denials with reasons
Grievance records related to access
Quarterly QI review

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment / Shared Housing Establishment (Administrator, Admissions staff, Nurse and the examining physician, PA or APRN)
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] admits only residents whose needs it can safely meet, that a comprehensive pre-admission assessment is completed by an authorized professional, and that admissions comply with the Act.
policies.policy: Before admission, a comprehensive assessment of the applicant's physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition must be completed by a physician, physician assistant (PA) or advanced practice registered nurse (APRN). After Public Act 104-0589 takes effect, an RN or LPN cannot complete this assessment. ILGA shows an effective date of July 24, 2026, and the Administrator confirms the date against the Public Act text. [AGENCY NAME] does not admit an applicant if it cannot provide or secure appropriate care, if the applicant needs a service it is not licensed for or does not provide, or if it lacks staff with appropriate numbers and skills. It also does not admit an applicant whose condition is so deteriorated that residency would be detrimental to the applicant or others, or who is dangerous in a way that cannot be eliminated. For applicants with cognitive impairment, [AGENCY NAME] uses a validated dementia-specific assessment tool. At least 80% of residents must be age 55 or older, and the Administrator confirms this before admission.

definitions.definition: The pre-admission assessment of the applicant's physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition completed by a physician, PA or APRN.
An additional assessment by [AGENCY NAME] staff (for example, the Nurse) that supports service planning. It does not replace the comprehensive assessment.
A cognitive assessment instrument validated for dementia-related cognitive impairment, with inter-rater reliability. IDPH rule identifies the standard.
The conditions in the Act and in the Department's residency requirements that determine whether [AGENCY NAME] may accept or retain a resident.

procedures: The Admissions staff handle each inquiry using a standard Pre-Admission Screening Form ([FORM NUMBER]). It records the applicant's age, diagnoses, medications, mobility, cognition, behaviors, continence, diet, skin condition, treatments, funding source and any need for hospice or skilled services.
The Admissions staff confirm the applicant's age. The Administrator confirms and documents that, with this applicant, at least 80% of residents will be age 55 or older (RR-08).

The Administrator and Nurse review the screening and decide whether to proceed. They check the applicant's needs against the Act's admission and retention criteria, the establishment's license, current staffing numbers and skills, and the conditions the establishment cannot serve (ADM-04). They document the decision on the screening form.

The Administrator tells the applicant and any representative which services [AGENCY NAME] provides, which are extra-cost services, and that Medicaid does not pay for services in this establishment, as the contract states (RR-04).

The applicant or representative arranges for a physician, PA or APRN to complete the comprehensive assessment and sign it before the admission date. [AGENCY NAME] gives them the Physician's Assessment Form the Department prescribes. Because the form and the rule may not yet match the Act's PA/APRN language, the Administrator asks IDPH in writing which form version to use and keeps the answer on file.

On and after the effective date of Public Act 104-0589, the Administrator rejects any pre-admission comprehensive assessment that was completed or signed only by an RN or LPN, and requests one from a physician, PA or APRN. An establishment RN or LPN may complete a supplemental establishment assessment but not the comprehensive assessment.

For an applicant with known or suspected cognitive impairment, the Nurse or other qualified staff completes the validated dementia-specific assessment tool that IDPH rule identifies. The Administrator confirms that the tool is validated for dementia-related cognitive impairment and keeps the completed tool in the record.

For an applicant to a dementia program, the physician, or a PA or APRN with geriatric dementia experience, approves the dementia assessment before acceptance. The Administrator verifies and documents the experience of any PA or APRN who approves it.

The Administrator and Nurse review the completed comprehensive assessment, the dementia assessment where applicable, and the supplemental establishment assessment. They look for any condition or need that would bar admission: a need for services the establishment is not licensed for or does not provide, a need that cannot be met by appropriately skilled staff, a condition that makes residency detrimental to the applicant or others, or danger that cannot be eliminated.
The Administrator checks the Act's resident admission criteria again immediately before each admission, and documents the check and the date on the Admission Checklist.

If the applicant can be admitted, the Administrator and Nurse draft the initial service plan with the applicant and representative (ADM-03). The applicant and representative sign the establishment contract (RR-04) and the Administrator gives them a copy. The signed contract is kept at the establishment.

If a resident is admitted with a risk that [AGENCY NAME] cannot fully mitigate and the resident chooses to accept it, the Administrator addresses it through the Negotiated Risk Agreement process (ADM-06), where the law allows.

If the applicant cannot be admitted, the Administrator tells the applicant and representative promptly and in writing, with the specific reasons. The Administrator offers referral information for other settings and documents the denial (RR-08).
The Administrator does not admit a resident whose comprehensive assessment is missing, incomplete, or signed by an unauthorized person, even if the bed is vacant or the family requests it.

The Administrator audits every admission file within 7 days after admission for the signed comprehensive assessment, dementia tool where applicable, age confirmation, signed contract, representative designation (RR-09) and service plan. The Administrator documents the audit.
The Administrator reviews admission denials, assessment completeness and the 55+ composition quarterly in the quality improvement program (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Makes the final admission decision, verifies the authorized assessor, confirms the 80% age requirement and criteria, and obtains IDPH direction on the correct form.
Completes screening review, the supplemental establishment assessment and dementia tool where qualified, and advises whether needs can be met.
Completes and signs the comprehensive pre-admission assessment and, for dementia programs, approves the dementia assessment.
Collect screening information, maintain forms and communicate decisions.
