The Administrator posts a one-page reporting guide at the staff station showing which diseases are reportable, whom to call, the local health department phone number [LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENT PHONE], and who in [AGENCY NAME] must be notified first.

The Human Resources designee asks each new employee for documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis before the employee has direct contact with residents. The method, test, results and any follow-up are accepted according to IDPH rule and recorded in the personnel file (see STF-04 and STF-05).

If an employee's skin test or blood test is positive, the Administrator requires a chest X-ray and a written clinician statement before the employee starts or returns to work. The employee is also screened for symptoms and instructed to report symptoms immediately. Results are kept in a confidential medical section of the personnel file.

At admission, the Director of Resident Services ensures each new resident has tuberculosis screening documentation as required by IDPH rule, including the results of a tuberculin test or alternative documentation by a physician, and records it in the resident record. If screening is not complete, the resident is not placed with others until the screening plan is approved by the physician (see ADM-01).

Staff report to the nurse or Director of Resident Services right away if a resident shows symptoms such as a cough lasting more than 3 weeks, bloody sputum, night sweats, weight loss or fever, or if any resident or employee is diagnosed with a reportable disease.

If tuberculosis is suspected, the nurse notifies the physician under HCS-04. The resident is placed in a single room with the door closed and wears a mask when others are present, and staff use respiratory protection as directed by the local health department. The Administrator notifies the local health department the same day.

The Infection Control Coordinator reports reportable diseases and unusual clusters of illness to the local health department within the timeframe in the reporting guide, and notifies IDPH as required. The coordinator records the date, time, person contacted and instructions received.

The Administrator notifies the resident's physician and representative, and informs the resident, whenever a communicable disease affects the resident. Staff are told only what they need to know to protect residents and themselves.

Following a case of active tuberculosis or other reportable disease, the Infection Control Coordinator works with the local health department on contact investigation. The coordinator provides lists of exposed residents and staff and arranges testing and follow-up as the health department directs.

The Administrator excludes any employee with active tuberculosis or another communicable disease from work until a physician or the health department clears the employee in writing. A copy of the clearance is placed in the confidential employee medical file.

Employees with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials follow SAF-07 and 29 CFR 1910.1030 for vaccination, exposure reporting and post-exposure follow-up. The exposure report is kept separately from the personnel file.

The Human Resources designee reviews every employee file at least quarterly to verify that tuberculosis documentation is present, and reports missing items to the Administrator, who removes employees from resident contact until the items are completed.
The Administrator keeps reports, test results and correspondence with health authorities for the periods set in STF-05 and REC-01, and keeps medical records separate and confidential.
The Administrator reviews the program annually with the quality committee, including timeliness of reports, screening compliance and any outbreaks, and records corrective actions (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Verifies current rule and reporting requirements, ensures screening compliance, excludes ill employees and makes required reports.
Posts and updates the reporting guide, reports diseases to the health department and coordinates contact investigation.
Verifies resident screening at admission, assesses symptoms, notifies physicians and implements isolation.
Collects and files employee tuberculosis documentation and audits files quarterly.
Provide screening documentation, report symptoms and exposures, and keep disease information confidential.

documentation: Infection Control Manual with verified IDPH rule and local reporting requirements and verification date
Reporting guide posted at staff station
Employee tuberculosis documentation and clearance letters (confidential medical file section)
Resident tuberculosis screening documentation in the resident record
Communicable disease and outbreak report log with date, time, person contacted and instructions
Exposure incident reports
Quarterly personnel file audit records

policies.title: Physical Environment, Heat Safety and Maintenance
policies.applies_to: All staff, residents and contractors; assisted living and shared housing operations
policies.purpose: To keep the building, grounds, resident units and equipment safe, clean and accessible, and to protect residents from heat-related illness and other environmental hazards.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains the building, grounds, furnishings and equipment in accordance with the physical plant and environmental requirements in IDPH rules for assisted living and shared housing establishments, the Life Safety Code as adopted by IDPH, local codes, and the Americans with Disabilities Act where applicable. Resident units and common areas are kept clean, in good repair and free of hazards. Heat safety is an environmental requirement: the Administrator adopts written temperature and heat index thresholds and required actions consistent with the heat index (apparent temperature) table in IDPH rules, confirms them against the current rule text, and enters them in the Heat Safety Plan. Residents are protected from heat-related illness through monitoring, cooling measures, hydration and prompt medical attention. Maintenance requests and hazards are corrected promptly according to priority, and urgent hazards are corrected immediately.

definitions.definition: A measure of how hot it feels when air temperature and humidity are combined; IDPH rules include a table used to determine heat-related environmental safety actions.
The written plan listing the indoor temperature and heat index thresholds, monitoring methods and required actions during hot weather.
Scheduled inspection, testing and servicing of building systems and equipment.

A condition that poses an immediate risk to health or safety, such as loss of heat or cooling in extreme weather, a broken lock on an exit, exposed wiring, a water leak near electricity, or a fall hazard in a corridor.
Usable by a person with a disability, including a person using a wheelchair or walker, in accordance with the ADA and applicable codes.

procedures: The Administrator obtains the physical plant and environmental requirements and the heat index table from current IDPH rules and the Life Safety Code, and the local building code. The Administrator records in the Maintenance Manual the thresholds and required actions, the date of verification and the source.

The Maintenance Lead writes a preventive maintenance schedule covering heating and cooling systems, water heaters, plumbing, electrical systems, elevators, emergency lighting, exterior lighting, doors and locks, generators and water temperature. The schedule is reviewed annually and every completed task is logged.

Staff report hazards and repair needs on the maintenance request form or log the moment they are noticed. The Maintenance Lead reviews the log each workday, corrects urgent hazards immediately, and completes routine repairs within [NUMBER] days. Urgent hazards that cannot be fixed at once are barricaded or the area is closed and residents are protected until repair.

The Maintenance Lead tests water temperature at resident-accessible taps and showers weekly and adjusts the water heater setting to prevent scalding, at the limit set in the Maintenance Manual. Results are logged, and any out-of-range reading is corrected the same day.

Common areas, hallways, stairways and outdoor walkways are kept lit, dry and free of clutter. Handrails, grab bars and non-slip surfaces are inspected monthly. Spills are cleaned immediately, and snow and ice are removed from walks and entrances promptly.

The Administrator ensures that resident units have the furnishings, locks, call or alert systems, bathrooms and other features required by IDPH rules. The Maintenance Lead inspects each unit when a resident moves out and annually, and records findings and repairs.

The Maintenance Lead and Administrator review the building for accessibility, including entrances, doorways, corridors, bathrooms, and common areas, and correct barriers to the extent required by the ADA and building codes. Residents may request reasonable modifications, and the Administrator responds in writing.

The Maintenance Lead keeps each unit's and common area's temperature in the comfortable range set in the Maintenance Manual and in accordance with IDPH rules. Heating and cooling systems are serviced before each season. If a system fails, the Maintenance Lead calls the service provider immediately and informs the Administrator.

During hot weather, the Administrator or designee monitors the forecast and indoor temperature and humidity at least daily, and in extreme heat at each shift, at locations in the building including units without air conditioning. Readings are entered on the Heat Safety Log and compared with the thresholds in the Heat Safety Plan.

When a threshold is reached, staff carry out the actions in the Heat Safety Plan: encourage and offer fluids to residents unless restricted by a physician, close blinds, use fans and air conditioning, move residents to cooler areas, limit outdoor activity to cooler times and check on residents more often, particularly those who are frail, have dementia, take medications that increase heat sensitivity, or have heart or respiratory conditions.

Staff watch for signs of heat illness such as flushed skin, dizziness, confusion, weakness, nausea, rapid pulse or reduced urination. They tell the nurse or Director of Resident Services immediately. In suspected heat stroke or other emergency, staff call 911 and begin cooling measures, and the nurse follows HCS-04 for notifying the physician and family.

If the building cannot be kept within safe temperatures, the Administrator moves residents to a cooler part of the building or an alternate location under SAF-05, notifies families and representatives, and reports the event to IDPH as required by SAF-02 and REC-02.

Housekeeping, laundry and pest control follow DL-03. The Maintenance Lead contracts with a licensed pest control service and keeps the service reports. Chemicals are stored locked and away from food and medications.

The Maintenance Lead keeps hazardous items such as cleaning products, tools and sharps, locked and inaccessible to residents who could be harmed, especially in dementia areas, and ensures exits, windows and outdoor areas used by residents with cognitive impairment are secure as described in HCS-05 and SAF-03.

Before any construction, renovation or change in the use of space, the Administrator contacts IDPH for the required plan review and approval and does not begin work until approval is granted. The Administrator provides infection control, dust and noise protections for residents during any work.

The Administrator reviews maintenance logs, heat monitoring records, resident complaints about the environment and survey findings at least quarterly with the quality committee (GOV-04) and corrects any trends.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the building meets IDPH, code and ADA requirements, approves the Heat Safety Plan, obtains plan review before construction and reports environmental events.
Performs and logs preventive maintenance, water temperature checks and repairs, and monitors indoor temperatures.
Identifies residents at risk of heat illness, assesses symptoms and coordinates medical response.
Report hazards, offer fluids, check residents during hot weather and watch for signs of illness.
Keep the environment clean and safe and report damage or hazards.

documentation: Maintenance Manual with verified IDPH environmental requirements and Heat Safety Plan, with verification date
Preventive maintenance schedule and completed task log
Maintenance request log with date reported and date corrected
Water temperature log
Heat Safety Log with temperature, humidity and actions taken
Unit inspection records
Accessibility review and resident modification requests and responses
IDPH plan review approvals for construction or alteration
Pest control service reports

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment
policies.purpose: To make sure residents receive safe, nutritious, appetizing meals, and that special and therapeutic diets are ordered, prepared and served as the service plan and the practitioner's orders require.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides food service to residents as described in the establishment contract and in accordance with the food service requirements of the Illinois Department of Public Health's assisted living and shared housing rules (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295). Staffing is scheduled to cover food service, as 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(h)(4) requires. Every food service employee has an initial health evaluation before starting work. Therapeutic diets are provided only on the order of a licensed practitioner and are reflected in the resident's service plan. The agency does not accept or keep a resident whose dietary needs it cannot meet.

definitions.definition: A diet ordered by a licensed practitioner to treat a medical condition or nutritional need, such as a diabetic, low-sodium, renal, texture-modified or thickened-liquid diet.
Any employee who prepares, handles, serves or stores food or cleans food areas, whether employed directly or through a contractor.
Scheduled staff time sufficient to plan, prepare, serve and clean up meals and to assist residents who need help eating, as listed in the services staffing must cover.

procedures: Before opening and again at each annual policy review, the Administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms in writing the current food service requirements in the Department's rules (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295, food service subpart) and updates this policy and the kitchen procedures to match.

The contract and service plan state which meals and snacks are provided, the number of meals per day, and any extra-cost food services. Residents and representatives receive this information at admission.
The Administrator designates a Food Service Supervisor, [NAME/TITLE], who is responsible for menus, purchasing, storage, sanitation and kitchen staff scheduling.

Before a food service employee starts work, Human Resources makes sure the initial health evaluation is completed and filed in the personnel record. The employee may not handle food until it is on file.

Food service employees are trained on safe food handling, hand hygiene, cross-contamination, allergen awareness and illness reporting during orientation. Employees with symptoms of an infectious illness report to the Food Service Supervisor and are kept off food duty until cleared under the agency's employee health policy (STF-04).

The Food Service Supervisor writes menus in advance and posts them where residents can see them. Menus take into account resident preferences, cultural and religious practices, and nutritional needs. Substitutions are recorded.

At admission and at each reassessment, the Nurse or other qualified staff member records each resident's allergies, food preferences, chewing and swallowing ability, and diet orders in the assessment and service plan (ADM-02, ADM-03).

A therapeutic or modified diet starts only after a written or documented practitioner's order is on file. The Food Service Supervisor receives the order within one business day, and the diet card or diet list is updated at once.
Kitchen staff check the diet list before each meal. Staff who serve or assist residents check each tray or plate against the resident's diet and texture requirements.

Care staff give residents who need help eating the assistance described in the service plan, and report to the Nurse any resident who refuses meals, has trouble swallowing, or shows a change in intake. The Nurse handles this under the change-of-condition policy (HCS-04).

Staff keep food, beverages and cleaning supplies in separate, labeled, clean storage. Staff keep refrigerator and freezer temperature logs and follow the temperature and sanitation standards set by applicable rule. Anything out of range is corrected and documented the same day.
The Food Service Supervisor keeps menus as served, diet lists, temperature logs and cleaning schedules on site for review by IDPH surveyors.

The Food Service Supervisor reviews resident satisfaction with meals at least quarterly through resident council input, comment cards or individual conversations. Complaints go through the grievance policy (RR-02).
The Administrator reviews food service findings, including complaints, weight-loss concerns and sanitation issues, in the quality improvement program (GOV-04) at least quarterly.
If the agency cannot meet a resident's dietary needs with its staff and kitchen, the Administrator follows the retention and discharge policies (ADM-04, ADM-05).

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure food service is staffed, compliant with rule, and reviewed in quality improvement.
Plans menus, supervises kitchen staff, manages diet lists, storage and sanitation, and keeps records.
Records diet orders and nutrition-related changes in condition, and communicates them to the Food Service Supervisor.
Serve meals as planned, assist residents who need help eating, and report intake or swallowing concerns.
Confirms the initial health evaluation is on file before food service employees start.

documentation: Posted menus and records of substitutions
Diet lists and practitioner diet orders
Food service employee health evaluations
Food service training records
Refrigerator and freezer temperature logs and cleaning logs
Resident dietary assessments and service plan entries
Quality improvement review of food service

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment, with additional requirements for any dementia special care program
policies.purpose: To offer residents meaningful social, recreational, spiritual and cognitive activities that fit their interests and abilities and support their independence and well-being.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides a program of activities that reflects residents' preferences and abilities, and residents choose whether to take part. If the establishment offers a special program for residents with Alzheimer's disease or other dementia, the program provides cognitive stimulation and activities designed to maximize each resident's functioning, as 210 ILCS 9/150 requires. The Administrator checks the Department's mandatory services rule for any activity requirement and builds it into the activity program.

definitions.definition: Planned individual and group activities offered on a regular schedule, including social, recreational, physical, creative, spiritual and community activities.
Structured activities designed to engage memory, attention, language and reasoning, and to maintain the highest practicable level of function for residents with dementia.
An Alzheimer's or dementia program the establishment has disclosed to IDPH and to residents.

procedures: The Administrator designates an Activity Coordinator, [NAME/TITLE], and makes sure activity time is included in the staffing schedule.

Within 14 days of admission, the Activity Coordinator or a designated staff member interviews the resident or representative about past and current interests, routines, faith practices, hobbies, and preferred times of day. The results are recorded in the resident's record and used in the service plan.

The Activity Coordinator prepares a monthly calendar. It offers a mix of social, physical, creative, spiritual and community activities, includes weekend and evening options, and offers choices for residents with different functional levels.
The calendar is posted in common areas and given to each resident or representative. Large-print or read-aloud versions are provided for residents who need them (RR-08).
Staff offer in-room or one-to-one activities to residents who cannot or prefer not to join groups, including residents on bed rest, residents who are isolated, and residents receiving hospice.
Staff invite, encourage and help residents to take part but never require participation. A resident's refusal is respected and documented when it is a pattern.
Staff provide the assistance, transportation, adaptive equipment and supervision residents need to take part, as described in the service plan.

For residents in a special dementia program, the Activity Coordinator plans daily cognitive stimulation and functional activities suited to each resident's stage and abilities, using the dementia assessment results. Activities are structured and offered throughout the day, including at times of day when confusion or agitation is greater.
Staff in a dementia program receive dementia training (STF-03) that includes how to lead and adapt activities and how to respond to behaviors without restraint.
Activity staff record attendance and each resident's response, such as who attended, level of participation and mood, at least monthly for each resident and sooner when something changes.
The Activity Coordinator reports to the Nurse any resident who withdraws, becomes depressed, or shows new confusion. The Nurse handles it under HCS-04.

The establishment holds resident council meetings or another resident input process at least quarterly. Activity ideas and complaints are recorded, and the Administrator responds in writing or at the next meeting.

Outings and events off site follow the transportation policy (DL-04) and safety and elopement precautions (SAF-03). Staffing for outings is arranged so on-site coverage requirements are still met (STF-01).
The Administrator reviews the activity program, attendance and resident feedback in the quality improvement program (GOV-04) at least annually, and updates it based on the findings.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure the activity program is staffed, funded and reviewed, and that dementia program requirements are met.
Assesses interests, plans and posts the calendar, leads or arranges activities and documents participation.
Help residents attend and take part, and report changes in mood or behavior.
Takes the activity needs of residents into account in assessment and the service plan and responds to reported changes.

documentation: Resident interest and preference assessments
Monthly activity calendars
Attendance and participation records
Resident council minutes or feedback records
Activity entries in the service plan
Dementia program activity plans, if applicable
Quality improvement review of the activity program

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment
policies.purpose: To keep the building, resident units, common areas and equipment clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair, and to provide laundry services that protect residents' health and dignity.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides housekeeping, laundry and maintenance services as described in the establishment contract. Staffing is scheduled to cover environmental services, as 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(h)(5) requires. The physical plant is kept in compliance with the Department's environmental and physical plant standards (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295, physical plant subpart).

definitions.definition: Housekeeping, laundry, trash removal, pest control and routine maintenance needed to keep the establishment clean, sanitary and safe.
Scheduled inspection, servicing and repair of building systems and equipment before they fail.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Maintenance/Environmental Services Lead, [NAME/TITLE], and schedules housekeeping, laundry and maintenance staff so environmental services are covered every day.

Housekeeping staff clean common areas daily and resident units on the schedule stated in the contract, using a written cleaning schedule and checklist. Staff initial the checklist when tasks are done.

Housekeeping staff use products and equipment approved by the Administrator, store chemicals in locked or restricted areas away from food and medications, and keep safety data sheets on site. Staff are trained on chemical safety at orientation (STF-03).
Staff follow infection prevention procedures when cleaning bathrooms, handling bodily fluids and cleaning after illness or outbreaks (SAF-07).
Laundry staff wash and handle soiled linen and clothing separately from clean items, wear gloves, and wash hands after handling. Laundry areas are kept clean and organized.
Where laundry service is provided, staff label residents' clothing, return it promptly, and report lost or damaged items to the Administrator. Complaints about property go through RR-05 and RR-02.
Residents who do their own laundry may use the laundry area as described in the contract. Staff help if the service plan says so.

Maintenance staff inspect the building, grounds, furnishings, lighting, plumbing, heating and cooling and emergency equipment according to a written preventive maintenance schedule. Heat and cooling safety follows SAF-10.

Residents, representatives and staff report repairs to the Maintenance Lead using a repair request log. Hazards that could injure a resident are corrected or made safe immediately. Other repairs are assigned a target completion date and tracked to completion.
Maintenance staff test water temperatures at resident access points on the schedule set by the Administrator and adjust them as needed to prevent scalding. Results are logged.
The Maintenance Lead arranges pest control with a licensed provider and keeps service records on site.
Trash and soiled materials are removed on a daily schedule and stored away from food areas and resident living areas.
Contractors are told about resident safety, privacy and infection prevention rules before entering resident units, and the Administrator makes sure they sign in and out.

The Administrator reviews cleanliness inspections, maintenance logs and resident complaints in the quality improvement program (GOV-04) at least quarterly. Any building change or alteration is reviewed against Department design and construction requirements before work starts.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure staffing, budget and oversight cover housekeeping, laundry and maintenance, and that the physical plant meets standards.
Runs cleaning and preventive maintenance schedules, manages repair requests, vendors and logs.
Perform assigned tasks safely, follow infection control rules and report hazards.
Report spills, hazards and needed repairs right away.

documentation: Cleaning schedules and completed checklists
Repair request and work order log
Preventive maintenance schedule and records
Water temperature logs
Pest control service records
Chemical safety data sheets
Environmental staffing schedule entries

policies.title: Transportation
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment
policies.purpose: To describe how the establishment offers transportation, if it chooses to, how it is priced and disclosed, and how residents are kept safe when they travel or when staff leave the site.
policies.policy: Transportation is an optional service. If [AGENCY NAME] provides it, the contract lists the transportation service and its fee schedule, as 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2030(a)(8)-(9) requires. The establishment follows applicable Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements for any vehicles and for access by residents with disabilities. In a shared housing establishment, staff may leave the site briefly for a resident's emergency room trip or errands, but must first arrange for monitoring of resident safety according to the service plan, as 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(k) provides. No resident's transportation outing may reduce on-site staffing below the required minimum.

definitions.definition: Transportation the establishment provides or arranges for a resident, such as to medical appointments, shopping or community events, using agency-owned, leased or contracted vehicles.
The written list of charges for optional and extra services that is part of the establishment contract.
The arrangement, described in the service plan, that ensures residents remaining on site are checked and can obtain help while a staff member is briefly away.

procedures: Before offering transportation, the Administrator decides whether it will be provided directly, through a contracted service, or not at all, and records the decision.

If transportation is offered, the Administrator lists it in the contract with its description, limits (days, hours, distance) and fees, and includes it in the fee schedule. If it is not offered, the contract says so and staff direct residents to public, paratransit or family options.
Fee changes are given to residents or representatives in writing at least 30 days before they take effect, as the contract rules require (RR-04).

Residents or representatives request transportation using the sign-up process set by the Administrator, with as much notice as the schedule specifies. Staff record the request and confirm or offer alternatives.

Drivers hold a valid Illinois driver's license appropriate to the vehicle, pass the background check requirements for staff with resident contact (STF-02), and complete driver and passenger-assistance training. HR keeps the license and driving record in the personnel file.
The Maintenance Lead keeps agency vehicles in safe condition with a maintenance schedule, inspections and records. Vehicles carry insurance, a first aid kit, and emergency contact information.

Vehicles and procedures accommodate residents with mobility devices, including lift or ramp use and securement, in line with ADA requirements. Staff do not refuse transport based on disability if the vehicle can safely carry the resident.

Before a trip, staff check the resident's service plan for mobility, behavior, medication and supervision needs and make sure the resident has needed medications, equipment, identification and emergency contact information.
Staff never transport more residents than the vehicle has seats and seat belts for, and everyone uses seat belts or securements.
Trips are staffed so the establishment still meets on-site coverage requirements (STF-01). The Administrator does not schedule an outing if doing so would drop staffing below the minimum.

In a shared housing establishment, before a staff member leaves for an emergency room trip or errand, the staff member tells the Administrator or on-call supervisor. They confirm and document how resident safety will be monitored while the site is staffed by fewer people, as the service plans provide, and arrange backup staff if needed.
Staff accompanying a resident to an emergency room follow HCS-04 and notify the representative. Staff return to the site as soon as the resident is stable or another responsible person takes over.
Staff report any accident, injury, behavior event or vehicle problem during transportation to the Administrator the same day and document it under SAF-02.

Staff keep trip logs listing date, driver, passengers, destination and times. The Administrator reviews the logs, vehicle records and any incidents in the quality improvement program (GOV-04) at least annually.

responsibilities.duty: Decides what transportation is offered, makes sure it is in the contract with fees, and makes sure staffing minimums are protected.
Maintain valid licenses, follow safe driving and passenger assistance procedures and log trips.
Identify transportation, supervision and safety needs in the service plan.
Maintain vehicles and records.
Approve and document staff absences from site and the safety monitoring arrangement.

documentation: Contract language and fee schedule for transportation
Transportation requests and trip logs
Driver license and background check records
Vehicle maintenance and insurance records
Documentation of safety monitoring arrangements for staff absences from site
Incident reports for transportation events

policies.title: Staffing Levels, 24-Hour Coverage and Supervision
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] always has enough qualified staff on duty, in number and skill, to meet residents' scheduled and unscheduled needs 24 hours a day, and to keep schedules that prove it.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains staff sufficient in number and skill to meet the 24-hour scheduled and unscheduled needs of residents, as 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(3) and 77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(a) require, and covers the services listed in 295.3000(h). The Illinois rules do not set a fixed staff-to-resident ratio, so the agency sets staffing by resident acuity and needs. An assisted living establishment keeps at least one staff member awake, on duty and on site 24 hours a day (295.3000(l)). A shared housing establishment keeps at least one staff member on site at all times (295.3000(k)). Residents who cannot move independently to safety are covered by sufficient awake staff 24 hours a day (295.3000(j)). At least one direct care staff person with current adult CPR certification, including a demonstrated skills check, is on duty at all times (295.3000(b)). The agency does not accept or retain a resident when it lacks staff appropriate in number and skill to meet the resident's needs (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.2000; 210 ILCS 9/150).

definitions.definition: Staff who provide personal care, medication assistance, supervision or other hands-on services to residents.
Alert, on duty and not sleeping, able to respond to residents at any time.
The record of date, scheduled hours and each employee's name and position, updated to show actual hours worked.

definitions.term: Residents who cannot independently reach safety
definitions.definition: Residents who cannot move to safety without help in an emergency, as determined by the assessment and service plan.

procedures: The Administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] sets the staffing plan before opening and reviews it at least monthly, and at once when census, acuity or services change. The plan states the number and type of staff for each shift.

In setting staffing, the Administrator considers the resident assessments and service plans, the services in the contract, meals and food service, housekeeping and laundry, medication assistance, activities, any dementia program needs, and the 295.3000(h) service list. Because there is no fixed ratio, the Administrator documents the reasoning behind each staffing decision.
In an assisted living establishment, the schedule assigns at least one staff member who is awake, on duty and on site every hour of every day. Sleeping on duty is not permitted.

In a shared housing establishment, the schedule assigns at least one staff member on site at all times. The Administrator decides, based on the assessments, whether any residents require awake staff overnight. If any resident cannot reach safety without help, sufficient awake staff are scheduled 24 hours a day.

In a shared housing establishment, a staff member may leave the site briefly for an emergency room trip or errands only after arranging monitoring of resident safety under the service plan and informing the Administrator or on-call manager (see DL-04).

The scheduler makes sure at least one direct care staff person with current adult CPR certification, including a skills demonstration, is on every shift. Human Resources tracks CPR expiration dates and removes the employee from the schedule as the sole qualifying staff member if the certification lapses.
The scheduler writes the personnel schedule before each period, listing the date, scheduled hours, and each employee's name and position, and posts or distributes it to staff.

The shift supervisor updates the schedule the same day to show actual hours worked, including call-offs, swaps, late arrivals and overtime. The schedule reflects who actually worked, not only who was planned.
The Administrator keeps personnel schedules for at least 12 months after the last scheduled date on the schedule and keeps them available for IDPH review.
Each shift has a designated person in charge who knows the residents who need extra supervision, how to reach the Administrator and Nurse, and the emergency plan.

The Administrator keeps an on-call list and call-off plan. When staff call off, the person in charge or scheduler calls replacements from the list, uses approved agency staff, or the Administrator or a qualified manager covers the shift. The minimum requirements above are never waived. If they cannot be met, the person in charge notifies the Administrator at once, who takes steps to secure coverage and records what happened.
Agency or temporary staff must meet the same background check, registry, training and CPR requirements as employees (STF-02, STF-03) and are oriented to the residents before working.
Staff who provide direct care or supervision are supervised by the Administrator, Nurse or designee, with the level of supervision appropriate to the tasks performed (HCS-03).

If the establishment has a special dementia program, the Administrator adds staffing and training suited to the program, as 210 ILCS 9/150 requires and the Department's rules for dementia programs set out, and records the dementia staffing pattern and emergency staffing plan.

If at any time the Administrator concludes the establishment lacks staff of the right number or skill to meet a prospective or current resident's needs, the Administrator does not admit the person, or begins the retention and discharge process (ADM-01, ADM-04, ADM-05).
The Administrator reviews staffing patterns, call-offs, resident complaints and incident reports about staffing in the quality improvement program (GOV-04) at least quarterly and adjusts the plan.

responsibilities.duty: Sets and reviews staffing, ensures minimum coverage is never breached and keeps schedules.
Prepares schedules that meet minimums and records actual hours worked.
Confirms coverage at the start of each shift, handles call-offs, and escalates shortfalls.
Tracks CPR and other required credentials and verifies staff qualifications.
Advises on resident acuity and supervision needs that affect staffing.

documentation: Written staffing plan with rationale
Personnel schedules showing date, hours, name, position and actual hours worked, kept at least 12 months
CPR certification tracking log
On-call and call-off records
Records of staff absences from site in shared housing and safety monitoring arrangements
Dementia program staffing pattern, if applicable
Quality improvement staffing reviews

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment
policies.purpose: To protect residents by making sure no one with disqualifying history or a registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property works in the establishment with resident contact.
policies.policy: All employees subject to the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (225 ILCS 46) meet its requirements, as a condition of licensure under 210 ILCS 9/35(a)(4). [AGENCY NAME] checks every applicant on the Nurse Aide Registry before hire and does not hire anyone with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property (77 Ill. Adm. Code 295.3000(m)). Fingerprints are collected electronically and sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days. Documentation of Background Check Act compliance and of the Nurse Aide Registry check is kept in each direct care employee's file (295.3000(f)(3)-(4)). The agency also verifies the licenses of licensed staff (295.3000(n)).

definitions.term: Health Care Worker Background Check Act
definitions.definition: The Illinois law (225 ILCS 46) that requires fingerprint-based criminal history checks and registry checks for employees who have, or may have, resident contact, and bars certain individuals from employment.
The Illinois Department of Public Health registry that lists certified nurse aides and records findings of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property.
A registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property, or a conviction that bars employment under the Act, unless a waiver is granted as the Act permits.
Any work that gives an employee, contractor or volunteer access to residents, their living areas or their records.

procedures: The Administrator [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] designates a Background Check Coordinator, [NAME/TITLE], who administers this policy. Anyone who works with resident contact, including direct care, food service, housekeeping, maintenance, activities, drivers and agency or contract staff, is covered.
Every job application and offer letter states that employment depends on passing the background check and registry checks. Applicants sign a written disclosure authorizing the checks.

Before any offer takes effect, the Coordinator checks the applicant on the Nurse Aide Registry, prints or saves the result with the date and the name of the person who ran it, and places it in the personnel file. An applicant with a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property is not hired.

For each applicable applicant, the Coordinator starts the fingerprint-based background check as the Act requires. Fingerprints are collected electronically by an approved vendor and sent to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days. The Coordinator records the date collected and date sent.
The Coordinator follows up with the vendor and the Department for results and tracks each applicant's check status on a log with the date started, date results received and the outcome.

No employee has unsupervised contact with residents until the Coordinator has confirmed the status of the check under the Act. The Administrator documents how supervision is arranged for any employee allowed to start before results are in, only where the Act permits.

If a result shows a disqualifying conviction or finding, the Coordinator tells the Administrator at once. The person is removed from resident contact, and is not employed unless a waiver has been granted as the Act allows. The Administrator documents the decision.

The Coordinator files proof of Background Check Act compliance and the Nurse Aide Registry check in each direct care employee's personnel file. Where the same checks apply to non-direct-care staff, proof is kept in their files too.

Before a licensed employee, such as a nurse, starts work, the Coordinator verifies the license is current and in good standing through the State's online verification, and keeps a dated copy of the result in the file.

Contract and agency staff are not allowed to work with residents until the agency provides proof of compliance or the establishment completes the checks itself. Proof is kept in the Coordinator's files.
Volunteers and students who will have resident contact are covered by the same checks, or are supervised at all times as permitted by the Act, with the arrangement documented.

The Coordinator re-checks the Nurse Aide Registry for employees who hold a certification, at least annually and whenever the agency receives information suggesting a problem. The Coordinator keeps the results.

If an employee is arrested, charged or convicted of a offense, or becomes the subject of an abuse or neglect investigation, the employee must tell the Administrator within one business day. The Administrator decides on actions such as removal from resident contact, as the Act and SAF-01 require.
Staff who are accused of abuse, neglect or misappropriation are handled under SAF-01. Reports to the Department are made as required.

The Coordinator keeps background check records confidential, limits access to those who need to know, and keeps them for at least the employment period plus 12 months as required for personnel records (295.3000(g), STF-05).

Before each annual IDPH review, the Coordinator audits all personnel files to confirm every employee has the required check, registry result and license verification, and reports the findings to the Administrator for correction (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure no one is hired or allowed resident contact in violation of this policy, and decides on any disqualifying result.
Runs registry checks, starts and tracks fingerprint checks, verifies licenses and maintains the log.
Includes check requirements in applications and offers and files the documentation.
Disclose accurately, cooperate with checks, and report arrests, charges or convictions within one business day.

documentation: Signed applicant disclosure and authorization
Nurse Aide Registry check results with date and initials
Fingerprint collection and transmission records, including dates sent to Illinois State Police within 10 working days
Background check status log
Documentation of Background Check Act compliance in each direct care employee's file
License verification records for licensed staff
Records of any removal from resident contact and waivers
Pre-survey personnel file audit

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: All employees, including direct care staff, the director/manager, and contracted or agency staff who work in the establishment
policies.purpose: To make sure every person hired by [AGENCY NAME] meets Illinois minimum qualifications, completes orientation before working independently, and takes ongoing training suited to the resident population, so that residents' scheduled and unscheduled needs are met 24 hours a day.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] hires only people who meet the written minimum education and experience in the job description. Direct care staff must be at least 16 years old when employment begins. Each new employee completes orientation before working independently with residents. Each employee takes part in ongoing training appropriate to the resident population served. Where [AGENCY NAME] operates a special dementia program, the director and all direct care staff also complete dementia and cognitive deficit training with the content required by IDPH rule. Orientation and training are documented in each employee's file. No one is hired until the required background checks and the Nurse Aide Registry check are complete (see STF-02), and licenses are verified for positions that require them. Orientation content and minimum hours follow the current IDPH rule on personnel training. The Administrator confirms them against the current rule text each year.

definitions.definition: Employees who provide hands-on assistance, supervision or personal care to residents.

The initial training given to each new employee before independent work. It covers the establishment, its policies and procedures, resident rights, emergency procedures, abuse reporting and the job duties.
Continuing in-service education provided after orientation and suited to the needs of the residents served.
Training on dementia and cognitive deficits required for the director and direct care staff of an establishment that offers a special dementia program.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a written job description for every position. Each states minimum education, experience, licensure or certification, and duties. Job descriptions are reviewed at least annually and when a position changes.
Before posting a direct care position, the Administrator confirms that the posting and screening criteria include the minimum age of 16 at hire and any CPR requirement for the position.
The hiring manager verifies each applicant's education, experience and references against the job description and records the results in the applicant file before an offer is made.

The designated staff member completes the Health Care Worker Background Check Act process and the Nurse Aide Registry check before the start date (see STF-02). Anyone with a Registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation is not hired.

For positions that require a professional license (for example RN or LPN), the Administrator verifies the license with the issuing authority before the start date. A copy of the verification is placed in the personnel file.

On or before the first day, the new employee receives the job description, the Policy and Procedure Manual sections that apply to the job, and the resident rights list. The employee signs an acknowledgment, which is filed.

Orientation is completed and signed off before the employee works independently with residents. Content includes resident rights, abuse/neglect/exploitation reporting, emergency and fire procedures, infection control, confidentiality, incident reporting, and the service plans of the residents the employee will assist. The Administrator confirms the required content and minimum hours against the current IDPH rule.
Until orientation is signed off, a new employee works only alongside an experienced employee and is not counted toward required staffing.

Direct care staff who hold adult CPR certification are verified. If a direct care employee lacks current adult CPR certification, they complete a course with a hands-on skills demonstration. The certificate is filed (see STF-01 for the on-duty CPR requirement).

The Administrator sets an annual training calendar covering topics suited to the resident population, such as dementia care, falls, skin integrity, medication-related duties, infection control, fire safety and emergency preparedness, resident rights, and abuse and neglect prevention.

If [AGENCY NAME] operates a special dementia program, the director and every direct care employee complete dementia and cognitive deficit training. This is done at hire for new staff, and again as IDPH rule requires. Completion is recorded in the file.

Each training session is documented on a sign-in sheet that shows date, topic, trainer, length, and attendee signatures. A copy of each attendee's record is placed in the employee's training record in the personnel file.
Employees who miss a required session complete a make-up session within 30 days. The Administrator tracks overdue training monthly.
When a quality review, incident, survey finding or change in resident needs shows a skill gap, the Administrator arranges targeted training within 30 days and documents it.
The Administrator reviews the training matrix every quarter and reports completion rates and gaps to the governing body and the QI committee (see GOV-04).
Training and orientation records are kept for the length of employment and for at least 12 months afterward (see STF-05).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains job descriptions, ensures orientation and ongoing training occur and are documented, verifies licenses, and reports training compliance to the governing body.
Screens applicants against the job description, supervises new staff until orientation is signed off, and identifies skill gaps.
Delivers or arranges clinical and resident-care training and signs off on competency.
Completes orientation and all assigned training and signs acknowledgments.

documentation: Job descriptions for all positions
Applicant file with education, experience and reference verification
Signed orientation checklist and acknowledgment of policies
Training sign-in sheets and annual training calendar and matrix
CPR certificates and skills-demonstration records
Dementia training records, if a dementia program is offered
License verification copies for licensed staff

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All employees; initial health evaluation applies to direct care employees
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff by confirming that employees are healthy enough to do their jobs, are free of pulmonary tuberculosis, and are protected from occupational exposure to bloodborne pathogens.
policies.policy: Each direct care employee has documentation of an initial health evaluation in the personnel file. Each employee has documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis in the file. Tuberculosis screening follows the procedures required by IDPH, as set out in SAF-09. Employee health information is kept confidential, stored separately from general personnel information, and retained for the length of employment and at least 12 months afterward, or longer where state or federal law requires. [AGENCY NAME] also follows the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard for any employee who may have occupational exposure.

definitions.definition: A health assessment of a direct care employee by a licensed health professional, documented before the employee provides direct care.
Documentation, using the IDPH-required screening procedures, that the employee does not have active pulmonary TB.
A specific contact with blood or other potentially infectious material that results from the employee's duties.

procedures: During hiring, the Administrator informs each finalist that an initial health evaluation and TB screening are conditions of working with residents.

Before the first direct care shift, the direct care employee provides documentation of an initial health evaluation completed by a physician, PA, APRN or other licensed health professional. The designee reviews it for completeness.

Before the first shift, every employee provides documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis using the screening method and timing required under the IDPH procedures. The Infection Control Designee verifies this against SAF-09.
An employee who has not completed these items does not work with residents and is not counted toward staffing.
The Infection Control Designee tracks TB screening and health evaluation dates on a tracking log and checks it monthly.

An employee with symptoms of active TB or other communicable disease is excluded from work as set out in SAF-07 and SAF-09 until cleared by a licensed health professional. The exclusion is documented.

The Administrator offers the hepatitis B vaccination series to employees with occupational exposure, at no cost, within the time OSHA requires. An employee who declines signs a declination, which is filed.
The Administrator provides bloodborne pathogens training at orientation and yearly, and makes personal protective equipment and sharps containers available.

After an exposure incident, the employee reports it immediately to the supervisor. The supervisor arranges first aid and medical evaluation and follow-up right away, and documents the incident using the exposure report form.
The Administrator records exposure incidents in a confidential record. The employee's medical information is shared only with the people who need it and as the law permits.
Employee health records are kept in a locked, access-restricted file separate from the general personnel file.
Records are retained throughout employment and for at least 12 months after the last date of employment, or longer if state or federal law requires.
The Administrator audits a sample of employee files each quarter for current health evaluation and TB documentation and reports results to the QI committee.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures all employees meet health and TB requirements before working with residents and that records are retained.
Tracks screening dates, verifies documentation against SAF-09, and manages exclusions and exposure follow-up.
Do not schedule employees who lack required documentation and report exposure incidents.
Provide required documentation, report symptoms and exposure incidents, and use protective equipment.

documentation: Initial health evaluation for each direct care employee
Documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis
TB and health evaluation tracking log
Hepatitis B vaccination record or signed declination
Bloodborne pathogens training records
Exposure incident reports and follow-up records
Exclusion and return-to-work notes

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: All employees and personnel file custodians
policies.purpose: To keep a complete, accurate and confidential file for every employee, containing everything Illinois requires, so the establishment can show compliance at any time and during an IDPH review.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a personnel file for every employee. Each file contains the employee's name, date of birth, home address, Social Security number and telephone number. It also contains documentation of freedom from pulmonary tuberculosis, orientation and ongoing training, and the employee's start and end dates. Files for direct care employees also contain current CPR certification where applicable, the initial health evaluation, proof of compliance with the Health Care Worker Background Check Act, and the Nurse Aide Registry check. For licensed staff, a copy of the license verification is placed in the file. Files are kept throughout employment and for at least 12 months after the last date of employment or service, or longer if state or federal law requires.

definitions.definition: The record, paper or electronic, holding the employment documents required by Illinois rule and by this policy.
The personnel file of an employee who provides direct care, which holds the added items required for direct care staff.
The person designated by the Administrator to maintain and secure personnel files.

procedures: The Administrator designates a custodian for personnel files and a backup, and records the names in the document control log.
At hire, the custodian opens a file using the standard personnel file checklist. The file includes the employee's name, date of birth, home address, Social Security number and telephone number.
The custodian adds the job description, signed policy acknowledgment, start date, and the application and verification of references.

The custodian files documentation of freedom from pulmonary TB and, for direct care staff, the initial health evaluation (see STF-04). Medical information is stored in a separate confidential section.
The custodian files documentation of orientation and every ongoing training session as it is completed (see STF-03).

For direct care employees, the custodian files proof of Health Care Worker Background Check Act compliance and the Nurse Aide Registry check result (see STF-02). These must be in the file before the employee's first shift.

The custodian files current adult CPR certification, with documentation of a skills demonstration, for each direct care employee who needs it. The custodian logs expiration dates and gives a 60-day reminder.
For licensed staff, the custodian files a copy of the license verification from the issuing authority. Licenses are re-verified at each renewal date.
The custodian records the employee's last date of employment or service within 5 business days of separation.
Before each employee's first shift, the custodian completes the checklist and the Administrator signs off. Any missing item must be corrected before the employee may work independently.

Files are stored in a locked cabinet or in a password-protected system. Access is limited to the Administrator, the custodian, and others who need access for their duties. Access by IDPH surveyors is provided on request.

Each quarter, the Administrator audits a sample of files, with all direct care files audited at least annually. Missing items are corrected within 7 days, and results go to the QI committee (see GOV-04).

After an employee leaves, the file is moved to closed storage and retained for the period of employment plus at least 12 months, or longer if state or federal law requires. The destruction date is logged before secure destruction, and the Administrator approves each destruction.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures files are complete, secure and retained as required, and conducts audits.
Builds and maintains files, tracks expirations, and logs retention and destruction dates.
Provide accurate information and promptly report changes of address, name or phone number.

documentation: Personnel file checklist for each employee
Employee identification and contact information
TB, health evaluation, orientation and training records
Background check and Nurse Aide Registry check results
CPR certificate and expiration log
License verification for licensed staff
Start and end dates
Record destruction log

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, volunteers and contracted staff
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of conduct and professional boundaries for people who work with vulnerable older adults, protect residents from abuse, neglect, exploitation and boundary violations, and keep people with Registry findings from working in the establishment.
policies.policy: All staff treat residents with dignity and respect. Staff must keep professional boundaries with residents and their families, and may not exploit a resident's trust, property, money or dependence. Staff are prohibited from abusing, neglecting or exploiting residents. Anyone with a Nurse Aide Registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of resident property is not hired and is removed from employment if such a finding comes to light. Staff must report suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation or boundary violations immediately as set out in SAF-01. Violations lead to discipline up to and including termination and, where required by law, referral to the proper authorities.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a staff member's professional role from a personal, financial or social relationship with a resident.
Improper use of a resident's money, property, or person for staff gain, including borrowing money, accepting valuable gifts, or using a resident's belongings.
Conduct that crosses the line between a professional relationship and a personal one, even without harm intended.
A finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of resident property listed on the Nurse Aide Registry.

procedures: At orientation, each employee receives the Code of Conduct and this policy, signs an acknowledgment that they have read and understand them, and is trained on resident rights and abuse prevention (see RR-01, SAF-01).
Staff address residents by their preferred name, knock before entering, protect privacy during personal care, and honor resident choices to the extent possible.

Staff do not borrow or lend money, buy or sell items, accept gifts of more than nominal value, or accept bequests, power of attorney, guardianship or any role in a resident's finances. Staff who are offered a gift of more than nominal value decline it and tell the Administrator.
Staff do not use a resident's belongings, accounts, credit cards, telephone, vehicle or identity for personal purposes, and do not handle resident funds except under RR-05.
Staff do not engage in romantic or sexual relationships with residents, and do not engage in conduct that is sexual, demeaning, threatening, or intimidating toward residents.
Staff do not take residents off the premises, or visit them outside work hours, for personal reasons unless approved in advance by the Administrator and documented.

Staff do not post photos, videos or information about residents on social media or share them in any other personal way. Staff do not photograph residents without written permission and a business purpose (see RR-07).
Staff do not work while impaired by alcohol or drugs, and do not use tobacco or personal devices in ways that interfere with resident care.

Any staff member who sees or suspects abuse, neglect, exploitation, or a boundary violation reports it immediately to the Administrator or the manager on duty, and follows SAF-01 for reports to the state. If the Administrator is the subject of the concern, the report goes to [GOVERNING BODY CONTACT] at [PHONE]. Staff who report in good faith are protected from retaliation.
The Administrator immediately removes any accused employee from contact with residents while the matter is reviewed, and starts an investigation within 24 hours as described in SAF-01.

The Administrator verifies the Nurse Aide Registry for each new hire before the start date and re-checks the Registry for current employees as set out in STF-02. An employee found to have a Registry finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation is removed from duty immediately and employment ends.
Substantiated violations lead to corrective action, up to and including termination, with the action documented in the personnel file. The Administrator makes all legally required reports.
Annually, all staff review this policy and sign a new acknowledgment as part of ongoing training.
The Administrator reviews conduct complaints each quarter and reports trends, without resident identifiers where possible, to the QI committee (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Enforces the Code of Conduct, ensures investigation and reporting, removes employees with Registry findings, and documents corrective action.
Model the standards, watch for boundary concerns, and report immediately.
Follow the Code of Conduct, keep professional boundaries, and report suspected violations immediately.
Receives and acts on any concern about the Administrator.

documentation: Signed Code of Conduct acknowledgment at hire and annually
Orientation and training records on resident rights and abuse prevention
Nurse Aide Registry check results
Investigation records and corrective action in the personnel file
Gift declination notes
Quarterly conduct review summary for the QI committee

policies.title: Director/Manager Qualifications, Training and Coverage
policies.applies_to: The Director/Manager, any acting or backup director, and the governing body
policies.purpose: To make sure the establishment is led by a full-time director who meets Illinois qualifications, keeps required training current, and is covered by a qualified named backup whenever the director is away.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs a full-time director who is at least 21 years old and holds a high school diploma or equivalent, with the qualifying experience required by statute and IDPH rule. As a condition of licensure the director completes at least 20 hours of training every 2 years. If [AGENCY NAME] offers a special dementia program, the director also completes dementia and cognitive deficit training as required by IDPH rule. The governing body names a qualified backup to act when the director is absent. Qualification evidence, training certificates and the backup designation are kept in the director's file.

definitions.definition: The full-time person responsible for the day-to-day operation of the establishment and for compliance with the Act and IDPH rules.
The experience the Act and IDPH rule require of a director, as shown on the job description and verified at hire.
A named, qualified person who exercises the director's authority when the director is absent.
An Alzheimer's or dementia program that the establishment discloses to IDPH and residents.

procedures: Before hiring a director, the governing body writes the job description showing minimum age of 21, a high school diploma or equivalent, and the qualifying experience required by statute and IDPH rule.
The governing body verifies the candidate's age, diploma or equivalent, and experience with documents and references before an offer is made, and files the evidence in the director's file.

The director completes the standard hiring steps for all employees, including background checks and the Nurse Aide Registry check where applicable, health evaluation and TB documentation, and orientation (see STF-02, STF-03, STF-04).
The director works full time on a schedule posted in the office. The schedule shows the hours the director is normally on site.

The governing body names a backup director in writing. The backup must be an adult employee who has been trained on the manual, resident emergency procedures, and reporting requirements. The name and contact number are posted at the staff station.

When the director will be away from the establishment for longer than a normal work absence, the director tells the backup and the governing body beforehand. The backup is on call and reachable at [PHONE] at all times during the absence.

The director keeps a training log. At least 20 hours of training are completed every 2 years, and the director tracks the 2-year cycle date. The director chooses topics related to assisted living operations, resident care, resident rights, and regulatory compliance.

If the establishment has a special dementia program, the director completes dementia and cognitive deficit training with the content required by IDPH rule, at hire and as the rule requires, and files the certificate.
The director files each training certificate with the date, hours, provider and topic in the director's file within 7 days of completion.
At least 90 days before each 2-year training cycle ends, the governing body reviews the log. If the director is short of the required hours, a plan to make up the hours is set and documented.

The governing body reviews the director's qualifications, training log and the backup arrangement at least annually and before each license renewal, and records the review in the governing body minutes (see GOV-01).
If the director leaves or is unable to serve, the governing body immediately names a qualified interim director, notifies IDPH as required (see REC-02), and begins recruitment.

responsibilities.duty: Hires the director, verifies qualifications, names the backup, and reviews training and coverage at least annually.
Meets and maintains qualifications, completes required training, keeps the training log current, and prepares the backup.
Acts with the director's authority during absences and follows all manual procedures.

documentation: Director job description
Evidence of age, education and qualifying experience
Director training log and certificates showing at least 20 hours per 2 years
Dementia training certificate, if a dementia program is offered
Written backup designation and contact information
Governing body minutes recording the annual review
Director's weekly schedule

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, use or store resident records, and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To keep a complete, accurate, secure resident record that supports care, meets Illinois content and retention requirements, and is ready for review at the annual IDPH on-site review.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a record for every resident. The record contains the signed establishment contract, the comprehensive pre-admission assessment completed by a physician, physician assistant or APRN, annual and change-in-condition assessments, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the current and prior service plans. It also contains the resident-specific documents required by IDPH rule on resident and establishment records. The signed contract is kept on the premises for the whole residency. Records are kept confidential under the privacy practices in RR-07 and the HIPAA privacy standards, including 45 CFR 164.530 administrative requirements. They are retained for the period required by IDPH rule and any longer period required by other state or federal law. They are made available to the resident or representative on request, and to IDPH for its on-site review.

definitions.definition: The paper or electronic file holding the documents, assessments, service plans, orders, notes and agreements about one resident.

The assessment of a resident's physical, cognitive and psychosocial condition completed by a physician, physician assistant or APRN before admission, at least annually, and on a significant change in condition.
Any additional assessment the establishment itself completes to plan services.
The written plan of services mutually agreed to by the provider, the resident and any representative, and reviewed at least annually and when needs change.
The person designated by the Administrator to maintain, secure and release resident records.

procedures: The Administrator designates a records custodian and a backup, and lists them in the document control log. The custodian opens a resident record using the standard checklist on the day of admission.

Before the admission date, the custodian places in the record the comprehensive assessment by a physician, physician assistant or APRN. No resident is admitted until it is in the file (see ADM-01, ADM-02). If a dementia diagnosis is present, the dementia-specific assessment tool is also filed (see HCS-05).

On the admission date, the custodian files the signed assistance living or shared housing establishment contract. A copy is given to the resident or representative, and the signed original is kept on the premises throughout the residency (see RR-04).

The custodian files the signed service plan, advance directive documents or notice of their absence (see RR-06), the designated representative form if any (see RR-09), and any negotiated risk agreement (see ADM-06).

Staff enter care notes, incident reports, change-of-condition notices, physician communications and medication records in the correct section of the record on the day of the event. Entries are dated, timed and signed or electronically authenticated with name and title.
Staff correct errors with a single line through the entry, the date and initials. They never erase or obscure entries.

The nurse or designee files the annual comprehensive assessment and any change-in-condition assessment as soon as completed, and updates the service plan when needs change. Superseded versions are retained, not discarded.

Within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days of a request, the custodian provides the resident or representative with a copy of the latest assessment, any supplemental establishment assessment, and the service plan. The request and delivery are noted in the record.

Paper records are kept in a locked cabinet in a staffed, access-controlled area. Electronic records require unique user IDs and passwords, role-based access, audit logging, and backup. Records are not left unattended in common areas.

Staff access only the records they need for their job. Release of information outside the establishment requires resident or representative authorization, unless the law permits or requires disclosure, such as to IDPH, a hospital or a physician for treatment (see RR-07).

The Administrator keeps the records needed for the IDPH on-site review in an organized location, and the custodian reviews the file contents against the review checklist before each review (see GOV-06).

The custodian audits a sample of active resident records each quarter against the checklist for completeness of assessments, contract, service plan and signatures. Missing items are corrected within 7 days and results go to the QI committee (see GOV-04).
When a resident is discharged, transferred or dies, the custodian completes the record, adds the discharge or death documentation (see ADM-05, HCS-09), and moves it to closed storage within 30 days.

Closed records are kept for at least the period set in the IDPH rule on records, or longer if other state or federal law requires. The Administrator maintains a written retention schedule and the retention end date is written on each closed record.

Before destruction, the Administrator checks for a pending survey, complaint, investigation or legal hold. Records are destroyed by shredding or secure electronic deletion, and each destruction is logged and approved by the Administrator.

If the establishment closes or changes ownership, the Administrator arranges secure transfer or storage of the records for the full retention period and tells residents and IDPH as the law requires (see ADM-05, GOV-02).
