policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Establishment and Shared Housing Establishment licensed by IDPH. Sections on the HFS Supportive Living Program (SLP) apply only if [AGENCY NAME] is SLP-certified. Applies to the Administrator/Manager, designated Compliance Officer, Director of Nursing/Health Services, Human Resources and the Governing Body.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] files every report, application, disclosure and notice it owes the Illinois Department of Public Health (IDPH), the Illinois State Police, and (if SLP-certified) the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS). Reports must be complete, accurate and on time, and each filing must be traceable in the record.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will meet all state reporting obligations on time and keep proof of each filing. The Administrator/Manager is accountable for the Required Reports Calendar. The annual license renewal application and fee will be filed within the 120-150 day window before the license expires, as required by 210 ILCS 9/45. Because a license lasts one year, names the physical location and is not transferable (210 ILCS 9/35), [AGENCY NAME] will keep its license information current and will not operate at any location or under any ownership that the license does not cover. If [AGENCY NAME] offers an Alzheimer's/dementia special care program, it will file and keep current the special care disclosure document with IDPH (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7)). Incident and accident reports will be made in the form and within the timeframes set by IDPH rules. The Administrator will notify IDPH within 10 working days of any change of manager. Fingerprint-based background check submissions for covered employees will be made to the Illinois State Police electronically within 10 working days, as stated in the agency's regulatory research. If [AGENCY NAME] is SLP-certified, it will submit quarterly quality-metric reports through the HFS SLP portal. Where a deadline or form is uncertain, the Administrator will confirm it with IDPH (or HFS for SLP) before the due date. A reporting deadline is never missed because a rule was unclear. No report will contain false or misleading information, and no employee will be disciplined for making a good-faith report.

definitions.definition: The Illinois Department of Public Health, Division of Assisted Living, which licenses and surveys assisted living and shared housing establishments.
A master calendar kept by the Administrator/Manager listing every recurring state filing, its due date, the person responsible, the date filed and the location of proof of filing.
The period from 150 days to 120 days before the license expiration date, during which the renewal application and fee must be filed (210 ILCS 9/45).

A renewal that IDPH may grant, at the licensee's request, only if in the preceding 24 months there was no Type 1 or Type 2 violation, no inspection with 10 or more Type 3 violations, and no admission or retention of a resident in violation of Section 75 of the Act (210 ILCS 9/45). IDPH is not required to grant it.
The disclosure that an establishment offering an Alzheimer's/dementia special program files with IDPH describing that program (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7)).
Monday through Friday, excluding State of Illinois holidays. Used to count 10-working-day deadlines.

An employee or prospective employee with direct care or access to residents, their living quarters or their records, who is subject to the Health Care Worker Background Check Act (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(4)).

procedures: Within 30 days of adoption of this policy, and at each license issuance, the Administrator/Manager builds or updates the Required Reports Calendar. It lists the license expiration date, the renewal window dates, the dementia disclosure review date, the quarterly SLP report dates (if applicable), and the name of the person responsible for each item.

The Administrator reviews the Required Reports Calendar at least monthly and reports any item due within 30 days to the Governing Body or owner at its regular meeting. Completed filings are initialed and dated on the calendar.

Annual license renewal: the Administrator calculates the 150th and 120th days before the license expiration date and enters both on the calendar. The renewal packet is started no later than the 150th day. The target filing date is at least 15 days before the 120th-day deadline.

Before filing renewal, the Administrator confirms that the application is complete, that the license fee is included, and that the physical location, ownership and licensed capacity shown are accurate. Any change in ownership or location is discussed with IDPH before filing, because a license is not transferable (210 ILCS 9/35).

The Administrator files the renewal application and fee with IDPH in the renewal window. The Administrator keeps a copy of the application, the proof of payment and proof of delivery or submission in the Regulatory Filings binder (REC-01).

Two-year renewal: before each renewal, the Administrator and Director of Nursing/Health Services review the last 24 months of IDPH survey results and admission and retention decisions. They check for any Type 1 or Type 2 violation, any inspection with 10 or more Type 3 violations, and any admission or retention in violation of Section 75. If none exists and the Governing Body wants a two-year renewal, the Administrator requests it in writing with the renewal application. The agency understands that IDPH may grant or deny the request (210 ILCS 9/45) and will plan on annual renewal and budget accordingly.

Dementia special care disclosure: if [AGENCY NAME] offers or plans to offer a special program for residents with Alzheimer's or dementia, the Administrator files the disclosure document with IDPH before the program begins and as part of licensure (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(7)). The Administrator reviews it at least annually and whenever the program changes in staffing, training, physical environment, services or fees. The disclosure is provided to prospective residents and representatives as described in HCS-05 and ADM-01. If no special program is offered, the Administrator records on the calendar that no disclosure is required and does not advertise or market the establishment as a dementia program.

Incident and accident reports: staff complete an incident report for every incident or accident as described in SAF-02, and notify the Administrator or on-call manager immediately for serious events. The Administrator (or designee) decides the same day whether the event is reportable to IDPH. Anything involving abuse, neglect, exploitation, unexpected death or serious injury is also handled under SAF-01 and HCS-09. When in doubt, the Administrator calls IDPH, then documents the call.

The Administrator submits each reportable incident to IDPH in the form and within the timeframe set by IDPH rules, using the attachments and contact information in the IDPH incident reporting instructions. The Administrator keeps a copy of the report, the date and time sent, the method, and the name of any IDPH staff member spoken to. A reportable incident is not delayed to finish the internal investigation. Follow-up information is sent to IDPH when available.

Manager change: when the full-time director/manager resigns, is terminated or is replaced, the owner or Governing Body notifies IDPH in writing within 10 working days of the change. The notice names the new manager, gives the effective date, and confirms that the new manager meets the qualifications in STF-07. The Administrator confirms the current requirement with IDPH when the change occurs, because the exact rule is to be verified against the licensing rules at the time. The written notice and any IDPH response are kept in the Regulatory Filings binder.

The Administrator confirms that the new or acting manager is on site, that 24-hour coverage is maintained during the transition (STF-01), and that the manager's 20 hours of training every 2 years (210 ILCS 9/35) is tracked on the training record (STF-07).

Background check submissions: Human Resources starts the Health Care Worker Background Check Act process (STF-02) for each covered employee on or before the first day of work. Fingerprints are collected electronically and submitted to the Illinois State Police within 10 working days. Human Resources logs the date of collection, the date of submission, the transaction or control number, and the result date.

Human Resources checks the log weekly. Any submission not made within 10 working days, and any result not received, is escalated to the Administrator the same day. A covered employee is not left unsupervised with residents unless allowed by the Act and STF-02. All covered employees must meet the Act (210 ILCS 9/35(a)(4)), and any disqualifying result is handled as STF-02 directs.

SLP-certified establishments only: the Administrator or designee gathers the quality-metric data required by HFS each quarter, has the Director of Nursing/Health Services review it for accuracy, and submits it through the HFS SLP portal by the HFS deadline. Proof of submission is saved. Questions go to HFS at 1-844-528-8444 or HFS.SLF@illinois.gov.
SLP-certified establishments only: the QI Committee (GOV-04) reviews each quarterly report. Any metric showing a decline or concern is assigned an action plan with a responsible person and a date.

Quality check: before each filing, a second person (the Administrator for staff-prepared reports, or the Governing Body designee for Administrator-prepared reports) reviews it for accuracy and completeness and signs the filing checklist. Reports are never signed with information that the signer has not verified.

Late or incorrect filings: if any report is late, incomplete or found to be wrong, the Administrator contacts the agency concerned right away, files or corrects the report, writes a short explanation of the cause and the corrective step, and reports it to the QI Committee at its next meeting.

Survey readiness: before the annual IDPH on-site review and any other survey (GOV-06), the Administrator assembles the Required Reports Calendar, copies of the last renewal application, incident reports filed with IDPH, the dementia disclosure (if applicable), manager-change notices and background check logs so that surveyors can review them on request.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure the license is renewed on time, receives the monthly report on upcoming filings, decides whether to request a two-year renewal, and notifies IDPH of manager changes within 10 working days when the Administrator position is the one that changes.

Reviews late or corrected filings, quarterly SLP metrics (if applicable) and trends in reportable incidents.
